panels.title: CPU system %
panels.description: High system time with low user time points at kernel/EDR/filesystem work (fseventsd, endpoint agents), not your code.

panels.title: Load1 / cores
panels.description: Runnable + waiting threads per core. Above 1 work queues; the load/cores > 4 alert fires after 15m.

panels.title: Swap used %
panels.description: Percent of the swap currently allocated by macOS (swap files grow on demand), not of free disk.

panels.title: Data volume free
panels.description: Red below 1 GB, amber below 5 GB. Excludes APFS purgeable space, so Finder shows a larger number.

panels.title: CPU: who is using it (100 = one core, 18 cores = 1800)
CPU by process group
panels.description: macOS daemons = fseventsd, opendirectoryd, diagnosticd, mds/mdworker, backupd, WindowServer, kernel_task. kernel_task is not visible to unprivileged ps (always 0 here); its cost shows up as unexplained system CPU.

panels.title: Top processes now (groups, by CPU)
panels.description: ~name rows are the current top non-allowlisted processes; 'other' is the rest.

panels.title: Load vs cores
panels.description: Load above the cores line means runnable threads are waiting for a CPU.

panels.title: Memory (stacked) and swap
panels.description: Swap used is drawn as its own line, not part of the RAM stack.

panels.title: Paging and swap traffic
panels.description: Sustained swap-out means RAM is over-committed. Page-in is also normal file-cache traffic.

panels.title: Data volume free space
panels.description: Dashed lines mark the alert thresholds: 5 GB (warning) and 1 GB (critical).

panels.title: Suspect CPU (100 = one core)
panels.description: Each suspect on its own line so a single offender is visible even when the stacked chart is dominated by another.

panels.title: Docker containers by image (CPU, 100 = one Docker-VM core)
panels.description: From `docker stats`, sampled every 30 s. Top 10 containers plus an 'other' bucket. Golang test containers show up by image here.

panels.title: Host vs app: stapler-squad stall metrics next to host CPU (shared crosshair)
Host CPU busy %
panels.description: If this is pinned near 100 when the app's latency spikes, suspect the host.

panels.title: stapler-squad Go scheduler latency
panels.description: Time runnable goroutines wait for a P/thread. Rising together with host CPU busy means the OS is not scheduling the process.

panels.title: stapler-squad mutex wait
panels.description: Rises with the app's own lock contention. Flat while sched latency and host CPU climb points at the host, not the app's locks.
